item.title: River Weathering Data and Machine-Learning Workflows
item.description:
This GRID project output combines USGS river chemistry and watershed information to examine relationships between land cover and rock-weathering fluxes. The release includes derived data tables, watershed predictor objects, and R code linking geochemical inverse modeling with XGBoost, model interpretation, and uncertainty analysis.

The workflow estimates silicate- and carbonate-derived alkalinity fluxes and generates predictions across the contiguous United States. It provides an example of how compiled river observations and environmental context can support AI-enabled research.

Access and contents

View and download the archived data and code · Explore the GitHub code repository

Release detail Information
Repository creator Xiying Sun
Release date August 8, 2026
Release DOI 10.5281/zenodo.21846324
Contents R scripts and derived CSV/RData files
Download ZIP, approximately 26.8 MB
Repository resource type Software
Repository license CC BY 4.0

The archive contains geochemical flux estimates, watershed predictor objects, and merged analysis tables. Its README documents 27 study-specific watershed predictors and code for InveR modeling, nested cross-validation, SHAP interpretation, spatial prediction, and bootstrap uncertainty estimation. Follow the archived documentation for required inputs, local path configuration, R packages, and cluster-based steps.

The archived flux table contains 1,153 unique sites; the merged flux-and-predictor table contains 1,084. These are table-specific counts, not necessarily the sample size of each fitted model or the total number of GRID sites. The release’s derived annual and seasonal summaries should be distinguished from individual observations and from predictions generated by the modeling code.

Reuse and citation

Use the release DOI to identify this archived package. The underlying study workflow is described in the manuscript titled Human modification of land cover reshapes rock weathering fluxes across the contiguous United States.

Data and code: Sun, X. (2026). XiyingSun/weathering-ml-project: Initial release for manuscript (Zenodo) [Software]. Zenodo. https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.21846324.

item.title: ROcD-nGoM: A River–Ocean Database for the Northern Gulf of Mexico
item.description:
This GRID project output connects river and ocean information for the northern Gulf of Mexico. It includes river chemistry and discharge for 54 rivers, streams, and bayous, together with 17 chemical and physical ocean parameters from the Gulf of Mexico Coastal Ocean Observing System and MODIS and SeaWiFS satellite sensors.

The release distinguishes river observations from daily concentrations and fluxes estimated using the USGS WRTDS model. It provides data with outlier flags and cleaned monthly, seasonal, and annual aggregates. Consult the documentation for the sampling coverage and processing applied to each parameter.

Access and scope

Download the dataset on Zenodo.

Release detail Information
Repository creators Bailey Armos and Shuang Zhang
Dataset release November 17, 2023
Release DOI 10.5281/zenodo.10152141
Files ROcD-nGoM.zip, approximately 2.3 GB; includes the river-processing R script
Repository license CC BY 4.0

This is a regional product with defined source coverage, rather than an archive of all analyses conducted in the Gulf of Mexico. The repository release predates the associated article.

Citation and associated article

Dataset: Armos, B., and Zhang, S. (2023). ROcD-nGoM: A River-Ocean Coupled Database for the Northern Gulf of Mexico. Zenodo. https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.10152141.

Article: Armos, B., Zhang, S., Wen, T., Walker, E., and Daripa, P. (2024). A harmonized river-ocean coupled database for the northern Gulf of Mexico. Scientific Data. Published December 30, 2024. Read the data descriptor.

item.title: U.S. River Salinization and Alkalinization: Data from 226 Sites
item.description:
This GRID project output compiles dissolved sodium and alkalinity data with 32 watershed properties for 226 river monitoring sites across the coterminous United States. The accompanying study uses these data to model monthly-aggregated sodium and alkalinity fluxes and examine their relationships with human and natural watershed characteristics.

Access and scope

Download data and code on Zenodo.

Release detail Information
Repository creators Tao Wen and Beibei E
Dataset release May 15, 2023
Version 1.0
Release DOI 10.5281/zenodo.7937820
Files Codes_and_Datasets.zip, approximately 56 MB
Repository license CC BY 4.0

The 226-site scope and 32-property feature set describe this study, not the current GRID-wide inventory. Consult the repository files and article for observation coverage, processing choices, and model evaluation.

Citation and associated article

Data and code: Wen, T., and E, B. (2023). Datasets and codes for the peer review article “Human and natural impacts on the U.S. freshwater salinization and alkalinization: A machine learning approach” (Version 1.0). Zenodo. https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.7937820.

Article: E, B., Zhang, S., Driscoll, C. T., and Wen, T. (2023). Human and natural impacts on the U.S. freshwater salinization and alkalinization: A machine learning approach. Science of the Total Environment, 889, 164138. Read the article.
